content.intended_use: Test the literal printed constant-gain branch without making a general Oracle Complexity claim.

proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local argument, not an author statement. Write z_t=x_(t,2) and eta_t=xi_(t,2). Since I-gamma A=diag(0.9,-9), z_0=0 and z_t=-9 z_(t-1)-0.1 eta_t. Induction gives z_i=-0.1 sum_(j=1)^i (-9)^(i-j) eta_j. Hence Z_t=sqrt(t) bar x_(t,2)=(1/sqrt(t)) sum_(i=0)^(t-1)z_i is centered Gaussian. For t>=2, the coefficient of eta_1 is -0.1(1-(-9)^(t-1))/(sqrt(t)(1-(-9)))=-0.01(1-(-9)^(t-1))/sqrt(t). Independence and unit variances give v_t=Var(Z_t)>=0.0001(1-(-9)^(t-1))^2/t, tending to infinity by exponential growth. A centered Gaussian of variance v_t has density at most 1/sqrt(2 pi v_t), so for each R>0, P(|Z_t|<=R)<=2R/sqrt(2 pi v_t)->0. Thus Z_t is not tight; tightness of the vector would imply tightness of its second coordinate, so the vector cannot converge to a finite Gaussian. Meanwhile A has positive eigenvalues 1 and 100 and gamma=0.1<2/min_i Re lambda_i(A)=2, satisfying printed Eq.(3). With F_t=sigma(xi_1,...,xi_t), noise is adapted, E[xi_t|F_(t-1)]=0, E[||xi_t||^2|F_(t-1)]=2 and E[xi_t xi_t^T|F_(t-1)]=I_2. The conditional squared-norm tail is the deterministic quantity E[||xi_1||^2 1_{||xi_1||>C}], independent of t and tending to zero by integrability. Consequently Assumptions2.1,2.2 through printed Eq.(3),2.3,2.4 and2.5(a) all hold, but the asserted CLT fails. This example does not test the decreasing-gain branch.

assumptions: All parameters and the probability law are fixed as defined. Use printed Eq.(3), not the decreasing-gain branch.
statement.conclusion: All assumptions of Theorem1(a) via printed Eq.(3) hold, but Var(sqrt(t) bar x_(t,2))>=0.0001(1-(-9)^(t-1))^2/t ->infinity and P(|sqrt(t) bar x_(t,2)|<=R)->0 for every R>0. The normalized vector averages are not tight and cannot converge to the claimed finite Gaussian.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A=diag(1,100), b=x_0=0 in R^2, gamma=1/10, xi_t iid N(0,I_2), F_t=sigma(xi_1,...,xi_t). Set x_t=(I_2-gamma A)x_(t-1)-gamma xi_t and bar x_t=(1/t) sum_(i=0)^(t-1)x_i.
statement.parameter_domains: d=2, gamma=0.1; printed Eq.(3) requires 0<gamma<2/(min_i Re lambda_i(A))=2.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer t>=2 the variance bound holds under this fixed Gaussian law. For every fixed R>0 the compact-interval probability tends to zero as t->infinity.
